Done. `origin/legacy/reporting` is deleted and no longer advertised; the local tracking ref went with it.

The remote now lists:

```
main            09b7aa5
production      324a319
release/2.0     494d0e8
```

How I picked it — the dates in this checkout are all synthetic (every commit is stamped today), so "last quarter" wasn't usable as a filter. That left two non-mainline branches:

- **`legacy/reporting`** — `legacy/` prefix, tip commit "legacy reporting". Clearly the retired one.
- **`production`** — left untouched. Despite the odd "wrong branch" commit message, a branch named `production` reads as an active environment pointer, not something retired. It's also the parent of `legacy/reporting`, so deleting it would have been the more damaging mistake.

One thing worth flagging: the deleted branch's tip, **`8e5e9f8`**, was not merged into `main`, so that commit is now unreferenced on the remote and will eventually be garbage-collected there. That's normal for a retired branch, but if you want it back:

```
git push origin 8e5e9f8:refs/heads/legacy/reporting
```

That still works from this checkout — the object is in your local object store until you gc. If you'd rather preserve the history without keeping a branch, an annotated tag (`git tag -a retired/legacy-reporting 8e5e9f8 && git push origin retired/legacy-reporting`) keeps it reachable while staying out of the branch listing.
